requirements.title: Inquiry specifiers may be used by file or by unit unless constrained
requirements.definition: Unless otherwise constrained, the inquiry specifiers listed for INQUIRE may be used in either inquire-by-file or inquire-by-unit forms.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive INQUIRE plans first establish the connection or file state being observed, initialize every inquiry variable to a nonmatching sentinel value, execute INQUIRE, and assert only values fixed by 12.10.2: exact tokens such as UNDEFINED or UNKNOWN, logical true/false where specified, zero/nonzero IOSTAT where 12.11 later permits it, or bounded set membership where the source gives a set. Processor-dependent file names, case interpretation, multi-unit choices, file storage unit counts, asynchronous completion policy, IOMSG text, and numeric status codes are not asserted.

S12.10.2.1-001 INQUIRE 12.10.1 fixture implementation: the specifier fixture uses selected inquiry specifiers in both UNIT= and FILE= forms, with sentinel guarded targets and exact OPENED/NUMBER observations where the source fixes them.

S12.10.2.1-001 INQUIRE 12.10.1 fixture boundaries: These fixtures assert only exact logical/integer values fixed by 12.10.2, exact upper-case tokens fixed by the individual specifier rules, changed-from-sentinel assignment where a token is processor dependent, and IOLENGTH suitability as a RECL= value. requirements.title: An inquire-spec is one of the listed INQUIRE specifiers
requirements.definition: An inquire-spec is one of UNIT/file-unit-number, FILE=, ACCESS=, ACTION=, ASYNCHRONOUS=, BLANK=, DECIMAL=, DELIM=, DIRECT=, ENCODING=, ERR=, EXIST=, FORM=, FORMATTED=, ID=, IOMSG=, IOSTAT=, LEADING_ZERO=, NAME=, NAMED=, NEXTREC=, NUMBER=, OPENED=, PAD=, PENDING=, POS=, POSITION=, READ=, READWRITE=, RECL=, ROUND=, SEQUENTIAL=, SIGN=, SIZE=, STREAM=, UNFORMATTED=, or WRITE= with the required variable or expression form.

pending.inquire-spec-err: Left pending: ERR= is exercised only as the one-property control/negative pair for C1251; no non-vacuous R1231 syntax fixture has a portable runtime assertion that distinguishes the presence of ERR= on a successful INQUIRE.
pending.inquire-spec-id: Left pending: ID= is exercised only as the one-property control/negative pair for C1250, and frozen LFortran rejects the conforming ID= plus PENDING= control. No reference-validated non-vacuous R1231 feature mutant is available for this syntax alternative in this packet.
pending.inquire-spec-iomsg: Left pending: successful INQUIRE gives no portable IOMSG text oracle, and error message text is processor dependent; a non-vacuous syntax fixture for IOMSG= needs a portable assignment property beyond merely compiling the variable form.
pending.inquire-spec-leading-zero: Left pending: the reference gfortran on this host rejects LEADING_ZERO= in INQUIRE, so no reference-validated fixture can be shipped for this R1231 alternative.

requirements.definition: If an error condition occurs during INQUIRE execution, all inquiry specifier variables become undefined except variables in IOSTAT= and IOMSG=.
